title: Articles: a, an, the or no article

groups.instructions: Choose the correct option to complete each sentence. A dash (–) means no article.

questions.prompt: ______ unemployment is one of the most serious problems facing young people today.
questions.explanation: Abstract uncountable nouns used in a general sense take no article.

questions.prompt: The chart compares the incomes of households in ______ United States and Canada.
questions.explanation: Country names that include a word like 'States', 'Kingdom' or 'Republic' take 'the'. 'Canada' takes no article.

questions.prompt: It took her ______ hour to finish the report.
questions.explanation: The choice between a and an depends on sound. 'Hour' begins with a vowel sound because the h is silent.

questions.prompt: She is studying at ______ university in Melbourne.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with a 'y' consonant sound (/juː/), so 'a' is used.

questions.prompt: ______ elderly often need more support from health services.
questions.explanation: 'The' + adjective refers to a whole group of people: the elderly, the poor, the young.

questions.prompt: Electricity consumption reached ______ highest level in December.
questions.explanation: Superlatives need a determiner such as 'the' or a possessive: its highest level. A superlative cannot stand alone or take 'a'.

questions.prompt: I bought a laptop and a printer, but ______ printer stopped working after a week.
questions.explanation: The printer has already been mentioned, so the second reference uses 'the'.

questions.prompt: Many people believe that ______ smartphone has changed the way we communicate.
questions.explanation: 'The' + singular noun can refer to an invention or type of thing in general: the smartphone, the bicycle.

questions.prompt: My brother works as ______ engineer in a car factory.
questions.explanation: Jobs take a/an in English: She is a doctor; he works as an engineer.

questions.prompt: Children usually go to ______ school at the age of five or six.
questions.explanation: School, hospital, prison and university take no article when we mean their main purpose (going to study, not visiting the building).

groups.instructions: Write the missing article (a, an or the). Write ONE WORD ONLY.

questions.prompt: Mount Everest is {{11}} highest mountain in the world.
There was {{12}} unexpected drop in sales in March.
questions.explanation: A singular countable noun mentioned for the first time takes a/an, and 'unexpected' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.prompt: The river flows into {{13}} Pacific Ocean.
